content:
alex: na-west GPU pool is degrading fast — g4-pool-3 reports 85% util, multiple OOM evictions on inference-prod. Queue depth up x4 and p95 latency spiking. Can we shift traffic off na-west immediately?

maria: seeing the same in Grafana. p95 went from 120ms -> 480ms over last 5m. Suggest we reduce na-west weight and route critical low-latency traffic to na-east/eu-west.

lee: na-east has ~8 cold GPUs in reserve (spare-pool-2). Cold-start to warm-up takes ~60-90s, but we can accept higher weight there once warmed.

anika: prepping a quick GSLB weight change. Plan: reduce na-west to 0.15, na-east 0.6, eu-west 0.25. Also enable model-variant fallback for heavy requests. Executing now: 
```
# gslb control CLI
gslbctl set-weights --region na-west=0.15 --region na-east=0.6 --region eu-west=0.25 --note "emergency steer: gpu depletion na-west"
```

ops-oncall: before you push, can you also pause batching on na-west to reduce token pressure? Command below.
```
infractl scale --service inference-batcher --region na-west --replicas 0 --no-wait
```

anika: applying both changes. pushing gslb policy, then scaling batchers. Will post IDs.

deploy-bot: gslb policy update accepted, run_id=run-20260317-89fa. Changing weights...
incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0457 (region: na-west, impact: degraded GPU capacity, severity: P2)

lee: starting reserve-pool warmup in na-east (spare-pool-2). ETA ~75s.

anika: gslb change completed. run_id=run-20260317-89fa ✅. New weights: na-west=0.15, na-east=0.6, eu-west=0.25.

alex: seeing immediate drop in queue depth from 1200 -> 320, p95 down to ~180ms. Nice. Thanks.

maria: verify that persistent connections / sticky sessions didn't keep clients pinned to na-west. If so, we need to restart the LB proxies for sticky TTL refresh.

ops-oncall: I’ll roll restart the proxy fleet in na-west one AZ at a time to avoid mass disconnects: `for az in a b c; do proxyctl restart --region na-west --az $az --limit 1; done`

lee: warmup done, instances healthy and registered. Traffic shift is stable so far. No new OOMs in last 2 mins.

anika: also enabled temporary autoscaler override: min_replicas=20 in na-east to keep capacity for next 30m.

alex: good call on autoscaler. Cost note: this will increase short-term GPU spend — flagging for finance/ops.

maria: follow-up actions: 1) telemetry sweep on kv-cache evictions, 2) investigate root cause of g4-pool-3 degradation (driver/kernel?), 3) consider adding a 10-GPU warm reserve in each region.

anika: logged root-cause ticket: INC-2026-0457-RCA and assigned to eng-runtime. Attaching grep logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] cuda: out_of_memory on worker-13 (g4-pool-3)
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] kube: evict pod inference-worker-13 (oomKilled)
[2026-03-17T14:03:01Z] autoscaler: no new nodes launched due to quota limit (project gpu-reserve)
```

ops-oncall: quota limit in autoscaler is suspicious — could be the quota bump for the account failed last week. Opening cloud ticket.

lee: if quota is the blocker we should request a temporary soft-quota increase, then drain returning traffic gradually back to na-west once nodes are provisioned.

alex: for now, keep weights as-is for 20-30m, monitor error budget. I'll notify product teams and CS about potential latency blips for some customers.

maria: sounds good. please add a perf-check at +15m and +30m to validate p50/p95, error rate, and queue depth.

anika: setting alerts: perf-check @ 1775012430 and 1775012645. Will update incident with postmortem stub.

deploy-bot: gslb policy applied successfully at 1775012360.

lee: current status summary: traffic shifted, reserve pool warmed, no new OOMs, queue at ~280, p95 ~160ms.

alex: thanks team. keeping this thread open until autoscaler/quota issue resolved and we verify healthy baseline. :white_check_mark:
